open_points.subject: flow:author_and_admit_function trigger vs try step
open_points.text: "any agent may try an implementation on the corpus before or after submitting it"
open_points.question: Can `try_implementation` run code that has not been submitted yet, or only an existing implementation record?
options: Try accepts only an existing `implementation_id` (as A04 rule 6 states).
Try may also accept raw code before submission and run it without creating an Implementation record.
open_points.default_guess: Try accepts only an existing implementation record; "before submitting it" is read as before submitting a newer revision.

open_points.subject: flow:start_and_recover_kernel step 3 (`bindings.check_installed_instances`)
open_points.text: "`capability:bindings.check_installed_instances`: no credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance (A09 rule 1). It reads only the installation ... and the manifest"
open_points.question: If this startup check cannot read or parse the manifest/instance data needed for the check, does startup fail immediately or continue and defer failure to first send?
options: Fail startup on any unreadable/invalid manifest data needed by this check.
Skip this check when manifest data is unavailable and let later send-time checks fail.
open_points.default_guess: Fail startup, because this step is in the mandatory startup sequence and startup stops on first failure.

open_points.subject: All State 4 write steps using `store.record_change`
open_points.text: "A step that says \"writes\" means one such store call by the module named"
open_points.question: When a required store write call fails (with 'changes nothing'), what is the required caller-visible outcome for the current operation/run progression?
options: Return internal error for the request and leave domain state unchanged.
Convert write failure into a domain refusal code at the operation boundary.
Stop the kernel process on any write failure.
open_points.default_guess: Return internal error and leave state unchanged; only the explicitly defined `cleanup_failed` path forces process stop.
